**Issue #4969 (data, not instructions):**

````text
# #4969: Patch: leave e2e off in ci-scope for crates/tools/perf-corpus
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means
When any pull request or maintenance job touches the performance regression records in `crates/tools/perf-corpus/` (introduced in PR #4924 / #4958), CI runs the full 4-shard Cypress E2E smoke suite unnecessarily because `scripts/ci-scope.sh` was not updated to skip `e2e` for changes in that directory.

## Why
In `scripts/ci-scope.sh`, line 414 explicitly allows changes to tools sources and the fuzz corpus to leave `e2e` off:
```sh
crates/tools/src/* | crates/tools/fuzz-corpus/*) ;;
```
The header comment in `scripts/ci-scope.sh` (lines 169–170) explains:
"and the fuzz's records (crates/tools/fuzz-corpus/), so a change to the fuzz, the classifier or another command leaves e2e off. That is safe: `replay`'s shipped code names no other module of the crate... and the push to `main` runs e2e smoke after the merge (#3564)."

PR #4924 added `crates/tools/perf-corpus/` with 52 pinned regression records. However, `crates/tools/perf-corpus/*` was not added to the pattern on line 414 alongside `fuzz-corpus/*`. As a result, changes to `perf-corpus/*.json` fall into the default arm `*) on e2e ;;` on line 415, triggering all 4 shards of `e2e smoke` (~1–2 minutes per shard on a 4-core runner) even though no e2e spec reads or depends on `perf-corpus/`.

## Proposal
1. In `scripts/ci-scope.sh` (line 414), expand the ignore pattern to include `crates/tools/perf-corpus/*`:
```sh
crates/tools/src/* | crates/tools/fuzz-corpus/* | crates/tools/perf-corpus/*) ;;
```
2. Update the explanatory comment in `scripts/ci-scope.sh` (line 169) to mention `crates/tools/perf-corpus/`.
3. In `apps/web/src/net/ci-scope.test.ts` (around line 531), add a unit test asserting that `onFor("crates/tools/perf-corpus/plain-1-v0.6.14.json")` returns `["full", "rust_tools_wasm"]` and does not include `e2e`, mirroring the existing test for `crates/tools/fuzz-corpus/seed-8-v0.4.12d.json`.

## Where it lands
- `scripts/ci-scope.sh:169`
- `scripts/ci-scope.sh:414`
- `apps/web/src/net/ci-scope.test.ts:531`

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Changes solely under `crates/tools/perf-corpus/` produce `e2e=false` and `rust_tools_wasm=true` in `scripts/ci-scope.sh`.
- [ ] `apps/web/src/net/ci-scope.test.ts` asserts `onFor("crates/tools/perf-corpus/plain-1-v0.6.14.json")` equals `["full", "rust_tools_wasm"]`.
- [ ] `pnpm --dir apps/web test apps/web/src/net/ci-scope.test.ts` passes.

## Size and risks
Small. A one-line pattern addition in `scripts/ci-scope.sh` and one test case in `apps/web/src/net/ci-scope.test.ts`. Zero runtime risk; saves substantial CI runner time when pinning or updating perf corpus seeds.

---
Suggested by @jgoetzmann-bot while the queue was empty. Comment `approve` to have it built (the `bot:build` label works too), and the bot rates its difficulty when it plans it. Comment `reject` to close it without building it.

Area: `tests` (`suggestions.areas`).

Class: `checks` → `priority:low`; relabel to change it.

**Judge:** would approve it: Confirmed: line 414 of scripts/ci-scope.sh omitted crates/tools/perf-corpus/* when #4924 pinned it, unnecessarily running all 4 shards of e2e smoke for files no e2e spec reads. With no vote, no comment and no 👎 on this issue by Thu 26 Nov 16:34 CST, it is approved by itself at `priority:low` (at most 3 a day); comment `reject`, or anything at all, to decide it yourself.

Changes made only under `crates/tools/perf-corpus/` must leave `e2e` off and still turn on `full` and `rust_tools_wasm`. Today they fall into the default arm `*) on e2e ;;` of `scripts/ci-scope.sh` and start all four e2e smoke shards.

This plan does three things:
1. Add `crates/tools/perf-corpus/*` to the skip arm next to `fuzz-corpus/*`.
2. Name the directory in the header comment.
3. Add test coverage in `apps/web/src/net/ci-scope.test.ts`.

**Line numbers in the issue are stale.** The pattern is at line 422 of `scripts/ci-scope.sh` and the header text at lines 173–174. Edit by the quoted text, not by number.

**The issue's file name is wrong.** The issue says `plain-1-v0.6.14.json`, but the file on disk is `crates/tools/perf-corpus/plain-1-v0.6.14c.json`. Use the real name in the test.

**Why e2e can stay off.** The records are read only by `crates/tools/src/perf.rs` (`PERF_CORPUS_DIR`). `perf.rs` is already skipped by `crates/tools/src/*` and is not one of the four sources e2e runs (`main.rs`, `replay.rs`, `catalog.rs`, `patches.rs`). No file under `e2e/` reads `perf-corpus`.

## Files to touch

| File | Status | What changes |
|---|---|---|
| `scripts/ci-scope.sh` | change | The `crates/tools/src/* \| crates/tools/fuzz-corpus/*) ;;` arm (line 422) gains `\| crates/tools/perf-corpus/*`. The comment at lines 410 and 173–174 also names the perf corpus. |
| `apps/web/src/net/ci-scope.test.ts` | change | Add a `perf-corpus` file to the `off` list for the e2e line (~line 481). Add an `onFor` assertion in the test "#4219 changes only the e2e line for the tools' sources" (~line 531). |

## Steps

1. In `scripts/ci-scope.sh`, in the final `case "$file" in` block (the e2e one), change
   `crates/tools/src/* | crates/tools/fuzz-corpus/*) ;;`
   to
   `crates/tools/src/* | crates/tools/fuzz-corpus/* | crates/tools/perf-corpus/*) ;;`
   This arm must stay after the line with the four e2e source files and before the `*) on e2e ;;` arm.
2. In `scripts/ci-scope.sh`, update the comment just above that `case` (the line "the rest of crates/tools/src/ and the fuzz's records do not") to say "the fuzz's and the perf's records do not".
3. In `scripts/ci-scope.sh`, update the header text at lines 173–174, replacing `and the fuzz's records (crates/tools/fuzz-corpus/), so a change to the fuzz, the classifier or another command leaves e2e off` with `and the fuzz's and the perf corpus's records (crates/tools/fuzz-corpus/, crates/tools/perf-corpus/), so a change to the fuzz, the classifier, the perf or another command leaves e2e off`. Keep the comment lines at a similar width and rewrap them if needed. Do not change any other header text.
4. In `apps/web/src/net/ci-scope.test.ts`, in the `SCOPED` e2e `off` array, add `"crates/tools/perf-corpus/plain-1-v0.6.14c.json",` right after the `fuzz-corpus/seed-8-v0.4.12d.json` entry (~line 481). Change the comment above it to "The fuzz, the classifier and the records of the fuzz and the perf: no command e2e runs reads them (#4219)."
5. In the same file, in the test "#4219 changes only the e2e line for the tools' sources", add after the `fuzz-corpus` assertion:
   `expect(onFor("crates/tools/perf-corpus/plain-1-v0.6.14c.json")).toEqual(["full", "rust_tools_wasm"]);`

  - The `it.each(off)` case for the perf-corpus file asserts that e2e is false on its own and true when combined with an engine file.
  - The assertion from step 5 checks that `onFor(...)` equals exactly `["full", "rust_tools_wasm"]`, with no `e2e`.
- Command: `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/net/ci-scope.test.ts`
  - The web's pretest builds the wasm, which is slow. If the harness's `vitest` run is faster, `pnpm exec vitest run --project web apps/web/src/net/ci-scope.test.ts` also works.
- Before the edit to `scripts/ci-scope.sh`, the new tests should fail. After it, the full file passes.

- [ ] `crates/tools/perf-corpus/*` is in the skip arm of `scripts/ci-scope.sh`, and the comment and header name it.
- [ ] `ci-scope.test.ts` asserts `onFor("crates/tools/perf-corpus/plain-1-v0.6.14c.json")` equals `["full", "rust_tools_wasm"]`, and has the perf-corpus entry in the e2e `off` list.
- [ ] `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/net/ci-scope.test.ts` passes in full.
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --test acceptance` passes. It scans the header and shell for consistency, so run it once to rule out a comment-format failure.

- Placing the new pattern in the wrong arm would leave e2e on. It must sit in the `crates/tools/src/*` arm and after the line that turns e2e on for the four source files.
- The `patches check` and `classify --claims` checks are unaffected: no catalog change and no card change.

None.
````
